channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Brown Bear Population in Spain Doubles With Incredible Increase of its Breeding Range
item.description: Cantabrian brown bears have doubled to about 370 in twenty years and now roam 6,500 square miles. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Indigenous students retrace Lewis and Clark’s historic journey: ‘We can’t protect what we cannot see’
item.description: Indigenous students are surveying wildlife along the Lewis and Clark route, two centuries on. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers have found a large icy body beyond Pluto that may become the sixth dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dr. King’s Lost Draft of ‘I Have a Dream’ Emerges from a Desk Drawer
item.description: A handwritten draft of the I Have a Dream speech has resurfaced after six decades in a desk drawer. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Man Rescues Trapped Neighbors from ‘Biblical’ Florida Flooding
item.description: A Florida man carried two vulnerable neighbours, one with ALS, out of fast-rising floodwater. How you can help: Check on neighbours who are ill or live alone when severe weather is forecast. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Infant Goes from 110 Seizures a Day to Seizure-Free with Experimental Treatment
item.description: A baby in Dubai who had about 110 seizures a day is seizure-free after an experimental drug. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is rebuilding tourism so that visitors help restore land and culture. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, pick locally owned stays and join a volunteer day if one is offered. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration
item.description: The National Trust is taking land back in hand to restore it and create new wildlife habitat. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two graduates have built a system that pulls microplastics out of water at treatment plants. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: China Switches on World’s Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage
item.description: China has switched on the largest plant yet that stores renewable power as liquid air. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 100-Year-Old ‘Store Mom’ Surprised With Her First Birthday Party
item.description: Store staff threw a 100-year-old regular her first ever birthday party. How you can help: Learn the names of the regulars you see each day; a greeting can grow into a friendship. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘There’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the Closet’ – Words that Led to Painting’s Joyous Rediscovery
item.description: A Georgia O'Keeffe painting kept in a closet has been rediscovered during a family clear-out. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brave Teens Execute Paddleboard Rescue of Flooded Neighbors – ‘Faith in Humanity Restored’
item.description: Teenagers paddled out on boards to bring a mother and son to safety when rescuers could not reach them. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions in 235 milliseconds, about twice as fast as humans. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: An AI model now predicts what a blind man with a brain implant will see, sharpening bionic vision. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A well-known tropical butterfly turns out to be three species, one of them new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
item.description: Experiments suggest Earth made its own water, hundreds of oceans' worth, in its hot early atmosphere. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A German designer is growing moss panels that cool streets and filter city air. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: After a decade of pressure from residents, Los Angeles has banned oil drilling within the city. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Go to a local council meeting; steady pressure from residents is what moved this decision. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: For Centuries, Visitors Walked Right by 280 Unseen Ice Age Cave Paintings
item.description: About 280 Ice Age engravings were found in a Spanish cave that visitors had walked past for centuries. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘I pulled him out, I heard more screaming’ – How a Cadet Saved a Father and Son from Drowning
item.description: A merchant marine cadet pulled a father and his son from a pool and both survived. How you can help: Take a CPR and water-safety class; trained bystanders are often first on the scene. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paralysis Could Not Stop Her: How This 84-year-old Made Good on Her Musical Promise
item.description: An 84-year-old who recovered from paralysis now plays piano for patients at the home that treated her. How you can help: Ask a local care home whether it welcomes volunteers who can play music or visit. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
item.description: Each mosquito species follows its own mix of skin scents, a lead for better-targeted repellents. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
item.description: Fossils from Thailand show a 66-pound rodent lived 34 million years ago, earlier than thought. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
item.description: Fossils from China reveal an armoured amphibian that lived in the sea 237 million years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: A young man who lost schooling in lockdown now runs peer tutoring for refugee students. How you can help: Offer an hour a week of tutoring through a local school or refugee support group. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil releases the world’s first fossil fuel phaseout roadmap
item.description: Brazil has published the first national roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
item.description: A new way of cleaning James Webb images has revealed a planet that was hidden in the glare. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ‘Nothing short of a miracle’ – Rescuers Find Boy with Autism Missing for 3 Days
item.description: A six-year-old autistic boy missing for three days in Kentucky was found safe by volunteer searchers. How you can help: Ask your local search and rescue team how to train as a volunteer. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers gave more than $76,000 to a full-time caregiver after a doorbell video showed her kindness. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World’s Driest Desert Erupts into Record-Breaking Bloom Boom (LOOK)
item.description: Rare rain has brought about 200 plant species into flower across Chile's Atacama Desert. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
item.description: A 450-million-year-old relative of the starfish has been found with its soft tissue preserved. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four volunteers have walked out healthy after more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
item.description: After a 40-year search, CERN has evidence of a particle decay that happens once in 10 billion. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric hydrofoil ferries that rise above the water are starting service in US cities. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Man’s Halloween Skeletons Prove Perfect Treat to Woman Battling Breast Cancer
item.description: A man's yard of Halloween skeletons became a weekly lift for a woman driving to cancer treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Rural colleges are adding play corners, childcare help and flexible advising so student parents can finish. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A UCLA study found a natural molecule may ease the brain fog that lingers after breast cancer treatment. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
item.description: NASA has set out a plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with an orbital test in 2027. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, where little can be farmed, neighbours keep each other fed by sharing what they catch and grow. How you can help: Share surplus garden produce with neighbours, or start a food swap on your street. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Spark: When Communities Own the Land, Housing Stays Affordable
item.description: Community land trusts are keeping homes affordable by holding the land under them for good. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Find out whether your area has a community land trust and go to one of its open meetings. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: A Montana guest ranch employs autistic people as wranglers, guides, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Back the businesses near you that hire neurodivergent staff. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish farmers in the US are building community around working the land. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants to safety so its Victorian Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
